items.title: $35K in stolen clothes and retail items leads to charges for Mississauga man
items.summary: Police say a Mississauga man stole items worth $50 to $4,000 in different thefts that added up to more than $35,000 and dozens of charges. The string of retail thefts happened across the Greater Toronto Area and Ontario, and Peel Regional Police say items were stolen in 38 separate theft-related incidents. Investigators launched an operation dubbed Project Bishop in April, and say all of the thefts were linked back to one “prolific” offender. Victims were identified in Peel, Halton and Durham regions, Hamilton, York, and the Niagara area, police say. Merchandise stolen in each incident ranged from approximately $50 to more than $4,000. Searches in Mississauga and Welland led officers to more than $35,000 worth of stolen merchandise. The pilfered items included cosmetics, and personal accessories, police say. Peel police say Anthony Orlando Monteith, 49, of Mississauga, was arrested on June 19 and has been charged with 24 counts of theft under $5,000 and 14 counts of possession of property obtained by crime. items.title: Candidates for mayor to square off in Mississauga debate
items.summary: Poverty, housing and food security will be among the issues discussed when Mississauga’s four main mayoral candidates meet on stage for the first major debate of the municipal election campaign in early October. Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network are co-hosting the mayoral debate on Oct. m. at FBM’s warehouse on Eastgate Parkway in the city’s east end. Organizers said the four top polling candidates — currently incumbent Carolyn Parrish, Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla — will be invited to take part in the debate. Participants will be confirmed by Sept. 18. The debate is being held “to ensure that poverty alleviation, including income and housing security, and food security are key platform issues for Mississauga mayoral candidates,” event organizers said in an online description of the upcoming debate. items.title: Port Credit Welcomes Craig's Cookies as Chain's First Mississauga Shop Opens Saturday
items.summary: According to INsauga, Craig's Cookies, a Canadian bakery chain known for fresh-baked cookies in unconventional flavours, is opening its first Mississauga location this weekend. The outlet reports the chain was founded by Craig Pike and got its start with a brick-and-mortar shop in Toronto's Parkdale neighbourhood in 2018. INsauga reports the new Port Credit location, at 102 Lakeshore Road east of Elizabeth Street, holds its grand opening on Saturday, August 29, with the first 100 customers receiving a free classic cookie. According to the outlet, the Port Credit store is owned and operated by new franchisee Imtiaz Hussain Bhatti. INsauga reports Bhatti lives in Oakville with his wife, Asma Safdar, and their two children, and the family often visits Port Credit.

items.title: Diesel and Premium Gas Prices Climb Again This Weekend Across the GTA
items.summary: According to INsauga, gas prices are rising across Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton, with the cost of regular, premium and diesel fuel all increasing on Friday and set to climb again on Saturday. The outlet reports premium gasoline rose by three cents on Friday in the Greater Toronto Area and is scheduled to go up another two cents on Saturday. INsauga reports diesel prices rose by one cent on Friday and are set to increase by another cent on Saturday. According to the outlet, the same upward trend is playing out across much of the rest of southern Ontario, not just the GTA. INsauga notes the back-to-back increases mean drivers across the region are facing higher costs at the pump heading into the weekend.

items.title: All collector lanes on the eastbound 401 closed near Mississauga Rd due to truck fire
items.summary: An early morning truck fire has shut down all collector lanes on the eastbound 401 near Mississauga Rd. and it is expected to remain closed for several hours.

items.title: OPP Shuts Down Winston Churchill On-Ramp After Highway 401 Truck Fire in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CityNews Kitchener, the Ontario Provincial Police closed the eastbound collector lanes on Highway 401 through Mississauga on Friday morning after a transport truck caught fire near Winston Churchill Boulevard. The outlet reports OPP said the closed lanes were expected to remain shut for several hours to allow for cleanup. CityNews reports the northbound Winston Churchill ramp onto the eastbound 401 was also closed, a step police took to keep additional traffic from entering the blocked stretch of highway. According to the outlet, OPP used the incident as an opportunity to remind drivers to slow down in the area while crews worked at the scene. CityNews reports the closure disrupted the Friday morning commute along one of the busiest stretches of highway in the Greater Toronto Area.

items.title: Stromedy Creator Kyle Godfrey Premieres Horror Short Simon Says at TIFF Lightbox
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga-based YouTuber Kyle Godfrey has released Simon Says, a 20-minute horror film centered on a remote cabin, a group of carefree twenty-somethings and an unsettling clown-like figure with unusual taste in party games. The outlet reports Godfrey, who has lived in both Mississauga and Milton, co-directs and stars in the film, building on earlier credits on Crated and The Mannequin Man. INsauga reports the film premiered at the TIFF Lightbox in Toronto last month, letting Godfrey move beyond the short-form videos he is best known for on his Stromedy YouTube channel. According to the outlet, Godfrey said he wanted to create stories with more depth and a real cinematic feel, contrasting the constant pressure of the next YouTube upload with the months spent building one story in filmmaking. INsauga reports Godfrey has built one of Canada's largest digital audiences over the years and has no plans to step back from YouTube despite the pivot into filmmaking. The outlet notes Simon Says is available to watch on YouTube and the streaming service Tubi.

items.title: Only Top Four Mayoral Candidates Will Take Part in Oct. 1 Mississauga Debate
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network will host a debate for the city's mayoral candidates on October 1 ahead of the October 26 municipal election. The outlet reports the event is organized to give candidates a chance to address income, housing security and food availability issues facing residents. According to a statement from the organizers, only the four candidates who are polling highest will be invited to take part, with the field confirmed by September 18. Mississauga.com reports the public can submit questions for the debate through an anonymous survey covering topics they want addressed, along with candidates' policy commitments and goals for their first year in office. The outlet reports that survey will also remain open until September 18. According to Mississauga.com, public registration for the debate itself opens in September, giving residents time to secure a spot before the event.

items.title: Cooksville Development Would Swap Two Houses for a Dozen Townhomes Near the QEW
items.summary: According to INsauga, a new development application submitted to the City of Mississauga proposes replacing two houses in Cooksville, north of the QEW, with 12 townhomes. The outlet reports the existing homes, along with any sheds or other structures on the properties, would be demolished to make way for the project, though the developer hopes to preserve mature trees along the rear and side lot lines. INsauga reports the townhomes would be split between two blocks flanking a common element condominium roadway, with access from Harborn Road. According to the outlet, five units are planned for the block on the west side of the private road and seven units for the block on the east side, with each townhome getting its own driveway and single-car garage. INsauga reports the driveways would have enough room to park an additional vehicle, and four visitor parking spaces, including one accessible space, are planned at the south end of the roadway.
